evidence.fact: The public ORCID record names Peter Mauch. It records Associate Professor at Western Sydney University (Humanities) from 2010. It records Assistant Professor at Ritsumeikan University (Faculty of International Relations) from 2006 to 2010. It records education at Kyoto University (Department of Contemporary History) from 2001 to 2004. It records education at University of Queensland (History) from 1993 to 2001. Exact identifier or specific full-title/date comparisons verify 34 graph credits against its public works list.
Publisher-deposited metadata names Peter Mauch as first author of the 1995 Hematopoietic stem cell compartment review.

Brigham’s 2017 memorial identifies Peter Mauch, MD, as a radiation-oncology leader whose clinical and research career there exceeded forty years; he died aged 70. This dated career distinguishes the clinical author from the ORCID claimant studying history in Queensland during 1993–2001.

reason: The 1995 stem-cell review is explicitly by Peter Mauch, fitting the separately documented Brigham radiation oncologist’s decades-long clinical career. evidence.fact: The public ORCID record names Hiroshi Shimizu. It records employment at Waseda University (Faculty of Commerce) from 2019. It records employment at Hitotsubashi University (Institute of Innovation Research) from 2008 to 2019. It records Ph.D at London School of Economics and Political Science (Economic History) from 2004 to 2007. Exact identifier or specific full-title/date comparisons verify 37 graph credits against its public works list.
Kyoto’s official English profile for agricultural-engineering Hiroshi Shimizu lists twelve specific full titles found among the graph’s linked credits, dating from 1993 to 2008.
The parallel Japanese faculty page identifies that Kyoto scholar as 清水浩 (Shimizu Hiroshi).

Waseda’s official entrepreneurship-centre organization dated September 2026 identifies its commerce professor as 清水洋, SHIMIZU Hiroshi, consistent with the ORCID claimant’s Waseda Faculty of Commerce appointment from 2019.

reason: Twelve linked works exactly match Kyoto’s agricultural-engineering bibliography for Hiroshi Shimizu, 清水浩, whereas the keyed claimant is Waseda’s commerce scholar, 清水洋. The different native names, institutions and documented works establish namesake contamination without treating every technical paper as foreign.

evidence.fact: The public ORCID record names Michael Egan. Exact identifier or specific full-title/date comparisons verify 0 graph credits against its public works list.
LC authority n2006073173 gives Michael James Egan, born 1974, McMaster History, and identifies his Barry Commoner research and 2004 doctorate.
McMaster explicitly links ORCID 0000-0002-9709-1206 to its associate professor of History Michael Egan.

The 1994 dopamine-metabolism paper’s publisher deposit names Farouk Karoum, Stanislaw J. Chrapusta and Michael F. Egan. The expanded author name differs from the key’s LC-identified Michael James Egan.

Publisher metadata for the 2018 verubecestat trial independently identifies Michael F. Egan at Merck Research Laboratories, documenting the clinical researcher rather than assigning a clinician identity from subject matter alone.

Georgia Press’s author biography identifies the McMaster scholar and explicitly names his book Barry Commoner and the Science of Survival: The Remaking of American Environmentalism. The exact book title is a key-log credit on p-39396.

reason: The dopamine article explicitly names Michael F. Egan, whereas the key’s LC authority expands the McMaster scholar’s name to Michael James Egan. The publisher also documents a clinical Michael F. Egan at Merck; this supports a foreign linked credit while leaving the other unverified clinical titles open.

scope_note: All current e_authored_f rows are listed, including hidden twins and credits under editorial roles. Counts are graph rows, not necessarily distinct intellectual works; not_theirs_count is a confirmed lower bound when unclear rows remain.

evidence.fact: The key has coauthor-mention anchors only. Publisher deposits identify Joe McEvoy and Oscar Zarate as authors of La théorie quantique en images and Stephen Hawking en images. Exact has-part DOI relations bind 166 graph chapter rows to these authored books; this is not an inference for an edited collection.
The Stephen Hawking book’s publisher deposit also names Joe McEvoy and Oscar Zarate and explicitly enumerates chapter DOI relations.

The public publisher book overview names J.P. McEvoy and Oscar Zarate for the very same Stephen Hawking title and DOI/ISBN, and credits McEvoy as a former researcher and science journalist. The shared exact work binds the Joe and J.P. forms; no nickname or initials-only identity inference is used.

EDP Sciences’ product metadata explicitly links paper ISBN 9782759812295 and electronic ISBN 9782759816972 under the same French quantum-theory book and J.P. McEvoy/Oscar Zarate credit, published October 2014. This supports the graph’s whole-book row even though its 2020 platform date is retained.

Icon’s catalogue verifies the English Introducing Quantum Theory: A Graphic Guide book by J.P. McEvoy and Oscar Zarate, eBook ISBN 9781848317574 (2014). The graph’s 2013 row is typed article, so this book metadata does not establish that row as the original work rather than a review.

Otago records the author’s 2007–2017 Waikato affiliation and lists the American and British world mission-history works he also claims in ORCID.
The public ORCID reports Otago from 2008 and claims exact works in the university’s bibliography.
NASA identifies this exact May 1971 tech brief as report MSC-13530, and the brief spells out its credit to Harry Doyle Morrison of Brown and Root-Northrop.
Optica prints H. D. Morrison at McMaster on the exact 1982 Raman paper, without expanding either initial.

reason: LC and Otago identify the keyed author as Hugh Douglas Morrison, while the exact 1971 NASA brief names Harry Doyle Morrison. The optics paper’s H. D. Morrison byline remains unresolved, and the NASA byline does not identify its author.

evidence.fact: The Geneva Graduate Institute separately names the scholar and lists this particular diary edition under her project director credit.

The 2004 Brill title page names Ṣadr-i Żiyā as the diarist, Rustam Shukurov as translator, Muhammadjon Shakuri as author of the introductory study and commentaries, Shahrbanou Tadjbakhsh as project director, and Edward Allworth as English edition editor.
The publisher’s contents distinguish the primary Diary beginning on p. 83 from its front matter and the appendices beginning on p. 381.
The publisher deposit for the exact Russo-Japanese War diary section repeats the edition contributors as authors. The title page and contents establish their distinct roles.

reason: Brill and the Geneva Graduate Institute identify Shahrbanou Tadjbakhsh as project director of the edition. The key log also credits her as author of primary diary entries attributed to Ṣadr-i Żiyā.

The publisher deposit for the exact Russo-Japanese War diary section repeats the edition contributors as authors. The title page and contents establish their distinct roles.

Columbia identifies its 1920–2016 professor, an alumnus and founder of two Central Asian studies programmes in 1970 and 1984.
Columbia’s memorial lists the dated books and expands the name to Edward Alfred Allworth.
Brill’s 2002 title page gives Edward A. Allworth for Evading Reality, with the exact graph LCCN in the publication data.
